record.paper_title: Initial boundary value problem for Korteweg-de Vries equation: a review and open problems
record.context_brief: Global well-posedness and blow-up for finite-interval KdV IBVP
record.original_question: For the Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval, let L > 0 and let u solve u_t + u_x + u_xxx + u u_x = 0 for 0 < x < L and t > 0, with initial data u(x,0) = phi(x). Impose three non-homogeneous boundary conditions B_i u = h_i(t), i = 1,2,3, where each B_i is a real linear combination of u, u_x, and u_xx evaluated at the two endpoints 0 and L: B_i u = sum_{j=0}^2 (a_ij partial_x^j u(0,t) + b_ij partial_x^j u(L,t)), with real constants a_ij and b_ij. Is this finite-interval KdV IBVP globally well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some s >= 0? Equivalently, can any solution blow up in H^s(0,L) in finite time, and can one establish a global-in-time a priori L^2(0,L) bound for such solutions?

evidence.quote: with general non-homogeneous boundary conditions posed on the two ends of the interval (0,L), (2.3) B1u = h1(t), B2u = h2(t), B3u = h3(t) t > 0

Is the IBVP (4.18) globally well-posed in the space Hs (0,L) for some s ≥ 0 or equivalently, does any solution of the IBVP (4.18) blow up in the some space Hs (0,L) in finite time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation on the finite interval (0,L), where L>0:
   u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0,   0 < x < L,  t > 0,
with initial condition u(x,0) = φ(x) for x ∈ (0,L) and three nonhomogeneous linear boundary conditions
   B_i u = h_i(t),   i = 1, 2, 3,   t > 0,
where each B_i is a real linear combination of u, u_x, u_{xx} evaluated at the endpoints x=0 and x=L:
   B_i u(t) = Σ_{j=0}^{2} ( a_{ij} ∂_x^j u(0,t) + b_{ij} ∂_x^j u(L,t) ),
with real constants a_{ij}, b_{ij} such that the three boundary functionals B_1, B_2, B_3 are linearly independent and the IBVP is at least locally well-posed in some Sobolev space H^s(0,L).

Question: For which choices of the coefficients {a_{ij}, b_{ij}} and which s ≥ 0 is this IBVP globally well-posed in H^s(0,L)? Equivalently, can solutions blow up in H^s(0,L) in finite time, and is it possible to establish a global-in-time a priori L^2(0,L) bound for solutions under these general boundary conditions?
artifact.status_search_result: Local well-posedness in H^s(0,L) for s≥0 has been established for general linear nonhomogeneous boundary conditions of this type, but a global a priori L^2(0,L) estimate is generally unavailable, since the L^2 energy is not conserved on the bounded interval even with homogeneous boundary data. Global well-posedness and the possibility of finite-time blow-up under general such boundary conditions remain open; only special classes (e.g., dissipative or specific homogeneous configurations) have been treated globally in the literature.

status_evidence.title: General boundary value problems of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded domain
status_evidence.snippet: Local well-posedness for general boundary conditions established; global L^2 estimate not available in general.
status_evidence.claim: Local well-posedness is known but global well-posedness for general boundary conditions remains open.

status_evidence.title: Global well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of a class of IBVP of KdV on a finite domain
status_evidence.snippet: Global well-posedness is obtained only for specific classes of boundary conditions yielding a priori estimates.
status_evidence.claim: Only particular boundary condition classes admit global-in-time control; the general case is unresolved.
